title: Adaptive latency-conditioned sampler and hotpath shield for ingress tracing hooks
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: During sustained high QPS (customer fleets and internal load tests) the tracer hotpath induces measurable allocations and mutex contention that elevate p50/p95 latency for inference requests. Existing route-aware prefilters reduce emitted spans but still require heap allocations and map lookups on the critical path. We need a low-cost, ingress-located sampler that: (1) makes sampling decisions with sub-microsecond overhead, (2) preserves a small, deterministic set of tail traces for posthoc analysis, and (3) surfaces metrics and tracing signals to the Console so Ops can correlate sampling behavior with latency/error dashboards.

Goal: Implement an "adaptive latency-conditioned sampler" that lives in the edge/proxy layer and uses tiny fixed-size reservoirs plus a latency-conditional skip heuristic. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration of lightweight hooks, dashboard telemetry, and a targeted perf regression test suite.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: ingress proxy hook, reservoir memory budget per-tenant, percentile-based sampling thresholds, export signal to tracing backend for rehydration, Console dashboard panels for sampler health and tail capture rate.
- Out of scope: changes to downstream storage backend, major schema changes to span payloads, or full rewrite of tracer SDKs (we will provide compatibility stubs).

Success criteria:
- Hotpath allocation overhead attributable to tracing drops by >= 60% in the 99th percentile path in synthetic high-QPS tests.
- Tail capture recall (for >95th latency events) >= 85% across synthetic workloads with skewed latency distributions.
- New Console panels show sampler decisions, reservoir fill-rate, and cross-correlation with latency/error metrics.

Design summary:
1) Decision prefilter: a tiny inlined heuristics unit that checks a 1-byte decision token and updates a per-request 8-bit skid counter, avoiding heap allocations.
2) Reservoir: fixed-size ring buffer per-ingress-shard (configurable at shard level), implemented with atomic indices and embedded minimal metadata (timestamp, request-id, sketch token).
3) Latency-conditioned retention: requests that cross configurable latency thresholds get higher synthetic sampling weight; errors always get promoted to reservoir.
4) Feedback loop: offline job computes latency percentiles and pushes small adjustments (delta thresholds) to the proxy via the control plane to adapt to workload shifts.
5) Dashboard signals: sampler_rate, reservoir_fill_pct, promoted_errors_rate, avg_decision_ns, tail_capture_precision.

Trade-offs considered:
- We choose a per-shard fixed ring instead of per-tenant dynamic memory to bound worst-case memory on the hotpath. This reduces per-tenant granularity but avoids allocations during bursts.
- We do simple integer math and avoid probabilistic heavy-weight RNGs on the hotpath; trade-off is slightly coarser sampling distribution but much lower overhead.

Implementation outline:
- Phase A (prototype): add inlined hook in the proxy binary, local ring buffer, and stubbed exporter to tracing sink (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3987).
- Phase B (integration): wire control-plane config, add metrics to the telemetry collector, add Console panels and alerting rules.
- Phase C (rollout): canary on devfleet, gradual ramp to production with knob to fully disable.

Testing plan:
- Microbench: synthetic QPS with and without sampler, measuring allocations, GC, mutex contention, and decision ns.
- Integration: end-to-end on devfleet with injected latency spikes and error injection to validate tail recall.
- Regression: integrate into CI perf suite (nightly) and add dashboard health check to catch regressions.

- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3987
- Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/tree/master/ingress-sampler
comments: 2026-03-02 | Ava Chen: Kickoff today. I implemented a first-pass inlined decision hook that returns a boolean without allocations. Benchmarked microbench with 1M reqs/s on devbox; decision cost ~120ns/op and no extra heap allocations. Next: wire reservoir and exporter stub.

2026-03-04 | Diego Martinez: Reviewed prototype PR. Requested changes: (1) switch atomic fence ordering to relaxed where safe to reduce stalls, (2) add a lightweight monotonic counter to avoid timestamp racy edge cases, (3) ensure request-id slice is not copied. See review comments in PR.

2026-03-05 | Priya Patel (Observability PM): Asked for Console UX acceptance criteria—please include the four panels and the alert thresholds. Also note we want an SLO-oriented query for tail_capture_precision < 0.8 to trigger review runbook.

2026-03-07 | Ava Chen: Prototype updated. After atomic ordering changes decision cost reduced to ~85ns/op on x86 instances. Allocations reduced by ~72% for the hotpath in perf-harness run (baseline: ~240KB/s allocs, now ~68KB/s). Added unit tests for ring overflow behaviour.

2026-03-08 | Security Review (note): Security looked at exporter stub—no PII stored in reservoir metadata; only request-id hashes and timestamps retained. We will add a config toggle to zero out request-id hashes for high compliance tenants.

2026-03-09 | QA: Integration test with injected 99th spikes shows tail_capture_recall 88% and precision 92% at reservoir size 128 per shard. Also observed a pathological case when many concurrent errors saturate reservoir; added backpressure heuristic to promote error eviction policy.

2026-03-10 | Ava Chen: Merged prototype PR to experimental branch. Next steps: add control-plane delta config push, expose metrics to telemetry collector, dashboard mocks for PM review. Planning canary rollout next week.
2026-03-10 | SRE Note: Need playbook entry for how to disable sampler quickly if a regression is observed. Adding runbook item to ops-playbooks repo.
